- When sentiment is negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast slope or shift mean down.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to account for subsequent mean reversion; cap forecast growth or add downward bias.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it — apply lagged correction or reduce forecast momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overestimate continuation; reduce forecast slope or add slight downward adjustment.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sharp drop, model underestimates risk — add early downward bias or adjust for sentiment volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near-term volatility; smooth forecast curve or reduce amplitude of short-term swings.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment, model tends to ignore it — apply stronger downward bias or adjust for sentiment decay.
